1. (Currently Amended) A golf tee comprising a long lasting combination of a golf tee and a force absorbing member in association therewith, said tee including a ground insertion end, a ball support end and a shaft in between, said member surrounding said shaft and being located below said ball support end and having an outer diameter less than that of a golf ball but large enough and located so as to protect said support end from impact from a golf club strike after a golf ball has been struck from said tee, __wherein said force absorbing member is permanently affixed to said shaft and is not slidable along the length of said shaft__.

2. (Original) The golf tee of claim 1, wherein said tee is formed from a material that enables the shaft to withstand damage from a strike on the resilient member.

3. (Currently Amended) The golf tee of claim 1, wherein said tee is formed from a member selected from the group consisting of __composite materials, fiberglass, carbon fiber, and__ wood, plastic and metal.

4. (Original) The golf tee of claim 3, wherein said tee is formed from a hardwood.

5. (Currently Amended) The golf tee of claim 3, wherein said tee is formed from an engineering plastic __selected from the group consisting of polycarbonate, nylon, polyetherimide, and polyetheretherketone__.

6. (Original) The golf tee of claim 5, wherein said tee is formed from a polycarbonate.

7. (Currently Amended) The golf tee of claim 3, wherein said tee is formed from nylon __having a tensile strength greater than 10,000 psi__.

8. (Original) The golf tee of claim 3, wherein said tee is formed from a malleable metal.

9. (Original) The golf tee of claim 8, wherein said tee is formed from aluminum.

10. (Currently Amended) The golf tee of claim 9, wherein said force absorbing member is formed from a force absorbing material comprising __a resilient elastomer selected from the group consisting of__ a natural or man-made material.

11. (Currently Amended) The golf tee of claim 1, wherein said force absorbing member is formed from a force absorbing material comprising __a resilient elastomer selected from the group consisting of__ a natural or man-made material.

12. (Currently Amended) The golf tee of claim 11, wherein said force absorbing material has a hardness of from about 30 to about 90 durometer __and exhibits a compression set of less than 25% after 70 hours at 70 degrees Celsius__.

13. (Currently Amended) The golf tee of claim 12, wherein said force absorbing material comprises a neoprene having a hardness of from about 50 to about 60 durometer __and a compression set of less than 20% after 70 hours at 70 degrees Celsius__.

14. (Currently Amended) The golf tee of claim 11, wherein said force absorbing material comprises a neoprene __having a durometer hardness of at least 40 and a tear strength of at least 200 psi__.

15. (Currently Amended) A method of making a golf tee for use when striking a golf ball, said method comprising the step of forming a long lasting combination of a golf tee and a force absorbing member in association therewith, the tee including a ground insertion end, a ball support end and a shaft in between, wherein the member surrounding the shaft is located below the ball support end and has an outer diameter less than that of a golf ball but large enough and located so as to protect the support end from impact from a golf club strike after a golf ball has been struck from the tee, __and wherein the force absorbing member is permanently affixed to the shaft and is not slidable along the length of the shaft__.

16. (Original) The method of claim 15, wherein the tee is formed from a material that enables the shaft to withstand damage from a strike on the resilient member.

17. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 15, wherein the tee is formed from a member selected from the group consisting of __composite materials, fiberglass, carbon fiber, and__ wood, plastic and metal.

18. (Original) The method of claim 17, wherein the tee is formed from a hardwood.

19. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 17, wherein the tee is formed from an engineering plastic __selected from the group consisting of polycarbonate, nylon, polyetherimide, and polyetheretherketone__.

20. (Original) The method of claim 19, wherein the tee is formed from a polycarbonate.

21. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 17, wherein the tee is formed from nylon __having a tensile strength greater than 10,000 psi__.

22. (Original) The method of claim 17, wherein the tee is formed from a malleable metal.

23. (Original) The method of claim 22, wherein the tee is formed from aluminum.

24. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 23, wherein the force absorbing member is formed from a force absorbing material comprising __a resilient elastomer selected from the group consisting of__ a natural or man-made material.

25. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 15, wherein the force absorbing member is formed from a force absorbing material comprising __a resilient elastomer selected from the group consisting of__ a natural or man-made material.

26. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 25, wherein the force absorbing material has a hardness of from about 30 to about 90 durometer __and exhibits a compression set of less than 25% after 70 hours at 70 degrees Celsius__.

27. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 25, wherein the force absorbing material comprises a neoprene having a hardness of from about 50 to about 60 durometer __and a compression set of less than 20% after 70 hours at 70 degrees Celsius__.

28. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 25, wherein the force absorbing material comprises a neoprene __having a durometer hardness of at least 40 and a tear strength of at least 200 psi__.
